SA on UK Red List

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Britain’s decision to leave South Africa on its Covid-19 red list of countries from which citizens may not enter the UK – while removing eight other countries from the list – has caused outrage. Families and business people in South Africa and the UK are shocked at this continued exclusion, especially in light of our rapid decline in infection rates. DIRCO Minister Naledi Pandor who has been working with our tourism sector and DIRCO to have South Africa removed from the red list said “ We firmly believe there is no reasonable basis for keeping South Africa on the red list.”
 


Further information:
Britain’s Transport Secretary Grant Shapps announced on Friday night that his government was removing Turkey, Pakistan, the Maldives, Egypt, Sri Lanka, Oman, Bangladesh and Kenya from the list and simplifying procedures for foreigners to enter. But SA stayed on the list despite furious campaigning by Pretoria and business to remove i.
David Frost, CEO of South Africa Tourism Services Association, Satsa, who has been leading the campaign on Shapps’ decision said it was “scandalous and completely unacceptable” and that the decision was based on obsolete Covid-19 infection data and bad interpretation of the science.
He said Shapps seemed to have based his decision on old information from last year that the Beta variant largely emanates from South Africa, which was anachronistic information dating from last December.  “We would want to know how Kenya was taken off the list. We know their genomic sequencing is just about nonexistent compared to ours. We do the good science,” Frost said, adding that he believed South Africa was unfairly paying the price for that science.
The UK imposed its outright ban on SA in December after SA had detected the Beta variant of Covid-19. Since then, the Delta variant has completely overtaken the Beta variant and is also dominant in the UK. Vaccines have proved very effective against this variant.
Britons who travel to SA have to endure 10 days of quarantine on their return, which has effectively killed the market, and is costing SA about R26-million a day, the tourist industry says.
The loss of British tourism has already cost SA R2.4-billion in lost revenue since it was put on the list in May, according to the World Travel & Tourism Council. The UK has traditionally been SA’s biggest source market for tourists. More than 430,000 British travellers arrived in SA in 2019.  During the complete shutdown of international travel from April to December 2020, UK arrivals dropped by 97%.
 
We look at the consequences of staying on the red list, what it means to our tourism industry and demand answers from the British High Commission.

Script:


 Link:  The UK governments decision to retain South Africa on its Covid-19 red list has caused a storm of protest not only from South African travelers but the nearly half a million UK tourists that come to our shores every year

V/O
So British tourists returning from South Africa, even if vaccinated, must quarantine  in a government-appointed hotel for 10 days at their own cost. Not a great incentive to holiday here

David: We were totally devastated, to be frank, gutted.. a lot of work has gone into this, a lot of interactions, data put forward the scientific arguments put forward the impact that this has had on the economy has been highlighted biggest market has been cut off from us.

V/O 6 sec
As CEO of Southern African Tourism Services Association David Frost, represents over a thousand in bound tourism companies.

Masa: Over 400 000 UK visitors annually to SA pre Covid what kind of expenditure are we missing out on right now?

David : We lose 26 million rand per day by being on this red list , the UK is our biggest single source the average spend per UK vistors is around 30 000 rand so these are massive losses.

Link: Being on the red list has a huge knock on effect on our tourism industry and the wider economy which supports one and half million jobs from travel agents, B and B’s, tour guides even crafters.

V/O 6 sec
Around one in seven South Africans put food on their tables, either directly or indirectly, through tourism.

David: Something that is particularly acute the emerging black businesss that have been growing over the last 10 years its great that we have had domestic tourism up and running but domestic tourism is generally not going into township tourism, town ship tourism if you will was really specifically fuelled and supported by the foreign market so those are small companies that don’t have cash reserves that don’t have strong balance sheets so they just fall away.

V/O 5 sec
Expats and families who are separated make up a large part of the inbound market, like Deon Gouws.

Deon Gouws
CIO Credo Wealth London
Deon: I came to visit my elderly mum she’s nearly 95 and on my return I was treated like every other traveler from red list country despite the fact I live in London and I was double jabbed in London on my return straight to the q hotel 10 whole days.

V/O
Costing Deon about 40 000 rand for bad food, no heat and limited access to fresh air.

Masa: You’ve been very expressive on twitter about your experience even calling it farcical?
Deon: Feel like criminal who needs to be locked up in prison and then the way that they treat you // every time you want to o out side you have to phone security so they can escort you because they are scared you might run away..denigrating in terms of your basic human rights.

LEON AYO
President
British Chamber of Business

Leon It has caused great distress families have not been able to see each other babies have been born people have been sick huge challenge emotionally but I think from a commercial and economic level its been disastrous.

V/O 9 sec
As President of the British Chamber of Business Leon Ayo, interacts with 600 members of corporates based in SA that rely on our travel industry

Masa: What are you saying to your members?
Leon: In the British Chamber we have the likes of Virgin Atlantic, British Airways we have got hospitality essentially been grounded over night 3 20 And I can assure you I spoke with the DHC this morning I spoke to the incoming HC this is top of our agenda here flying the flag fro Great Britain in South Africa

Marc Mendelson
Prof Infectious Diseases
University of Cape Town 

V/O
Marc Mendelson is Professor of infectious Disease at the University of Cape Town 

Masa Q Prof do you think there’s any reason whatsoever that can justify this decision?
Marc The reasons are a little bit baffling, so the red list countries are designated such because of a number of different criteria.  Our cases have dropped we are now down to to the bottom of our third wave, our vaccination programme is ramping up…

V/O
And very importantly South Africa has the capacity to monitor how the genome of the virus is mutating... 
and South Africa’s sequencing is extremely high level and far better than most of the countries that were taken off the red list.

Link :The British High Commissioner didn’t grant us an interview, issuing a statement saying in part 
……..We welcome recent positive developments in South Africa with cases going down, data on variants of concern improving and vaccination rising.  While a small number of cases, the continued presence of the beta variant in the community remains a concern given its potential ability to circumvent vaccines. 
 
Masa……… But scientists say this explanation doesn’t hold.

Mark; That is totally incorrect In September we have not had any Beta variant in this country to my knowledge between and certainly May to September we saw a massive drop in Beta currently our circulating strains causing infections in South Africa are the Delta strain not the Beta strain
If UK government were listening and looking at the data they would see our excellent scientific work in sequencing is now showing it’s the Delta Variant not the Beta variant so I think they are working on old data its not right and needs to change
V/O 
Last Friday eight countries including Kenya were removed  from the list of  the 64 red listed countries.

David: We spoke to people in Kenya they got off the red list and we asked them what did you do ultimately the feedback was we don’t know it goes into a black hole.

Masa to Mark We have higher vaccinated people in this country as opposed to Pakistan and Kenya who have been removed off the list?
Marc :Absolutely I think Kenya has 1. 6 % vaccinated Pakistan 10% we have have had over 15 million people receiving a vaccine so doesn’t stand up to scrutiny, love to be 100 % but not the case not near the case with the country’s taken off… scientists don’t make the policies ministers make policy and I think that’s where problem lies .

David That’s where the incredulity comes from its this feeling that there is not being supplied a consistent set of criteria. and some how SA is languishing on this red list position in a fairly pernicious and unfair way.

V/O
Following the intervention of our Government and the British High Commission, changes are now expected which should reflect in the UK’s review of the red list in 2 weeks time.

David..What is going to happen in the next couple of day is our top scientists are going to sit down with UK scientists and we are going to close this knowledge gap once our science is allowed to prevail the penny will finally drop…. we are hoping if we can crack that we can get travel between the two countries up and running again.
